NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Cloud Infrastructure / Platform Engineer
Manchester, UK | nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud infrastructure and platform engineer with 10 years of infrastructure experience, including 6 years operating Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Experienced in designing and running cloud environments, building Terraform-managed infrastructure, and leading platform initiatives from implementation through production. Focused on reliable, observable platforms and self-service infrastructure that helps product teams deploy and operate services effectively.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud and infrastructure: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), Terraform, Atlantis, Kubernetes, Linux, Puppet
Platform and delivery: Helm, Kustomize, Argo CD, Crossplane, Karpenter, GitHub Actions
Reliability and observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, SLOs and error budgets, incident management
Programming and testing: Go, Python, Bash, k6

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS)
Manchester / remote | Apr 2022 – Present
- Technical lead for a five-person platform team, operating an AWS EKS platform of 8 clusters and approximately 350 services across 3 regions.
- Built an internal developer platform with service templates, Argo CD GitOps, and Crossplane self-service provisioning for RDS, SQS, and S3; reduced the time to take a new service to production from approximately 2 weeks to under 1 day.
- Introduced SLOs and error budgets for the 20 most critical services, reducing on-call pages per week by approximately 60%.
- Moved node provisioning to Karpenter with spot instances, reducing EC2 spend by 38%.
- Serve in the incident commander rotation and established the incident and post-mortem process.

Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games
Leeds | Jan 2019 – Mar 2022
- Operated AWS game backend infrastructure using EC2, ECS, and later EKS for titles with up to 1.2 million daily active players.
- Managed AWS infrastructure as code with approximately 40 Terraform modules and used Atlantis for pull-request-based plan and apply workflows.
- Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, and Loki observability stack.
- Conducted pre-launch load testing with k6 and supported launch-day capacity planning.

Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting
Sheffield | Jul 2016 – Dec 2018
- Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration management.
- Automated infrastructure tasks with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer incidents.

EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016

CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021; renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional | 2023

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Urdu (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professional CV with a clear senior-platform-engineering profile. The summary is concise and relevant, the experience is achievement-led, and the quantified outcomes—such as reducing service launch time from approximately two weeks to under one day, reducing on-call pages by 60%, and reducing EC2 spend by 38%—make the contribution credible and compelling. The structure is easy to scan and the progression from Linux Systems Engineer to Senior Platform Engineer is clear. The main content limitation is not poor writing but incomplete evidence against this particular role: the CV does not demonstrate mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, security, Terragrunt, stakeholder engagement, or connected-device/IoT work.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly standard headings, reverse-chronological experience, conventional text formatting, and keyword-rich skills. AWS, Terraform, Kubernetes, EKS, Linux, systems observability, incident management, and platform engineering are likely to parse well. AI screening probability is high for general AWS platform, SRE, Kubernetes, and Terraform roles, but moderate for this specific vacancy because the document contains no Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, security, stakeholder, or system-design terminology. The skills section is well organised, although the most job-relevant capabilities could be made more prominent by placing Terraform and infrastructure architecture nearer the beginning and using a dedicated networking/security grouping only for skills genuinely supported by the candidate's background.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns strongly with hands-on infrastructure engineering, AWS cloud operation, Kubernetes platform ownership, Terraform-based infrastructure, observability, reliability, Linux, and technical leadership. The scale of the EKS platform, the internal developer platform, service self-provisioning, and incident leadership are particularly relevant to Corvale's end-to-end ownership and technology-first environment. The document also supports the role's need to help backend teams deploy and operate services effectively. Material gaps for this vacancy are strong Terraform and Terragrunt experience specifically, networking involving mTLS and SSL/TLS, certificate management, practical security awareness, explicit systems architecture/system design language, and stakeholder engagement with external engineering teams. The original candidate information does not provide evidence of IoT, automotive, remote-device integration, or JVM/backend development. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than CV-writing defects and should not be implied or added.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: None.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the existing architecture and technical-leadership evidence more explicit without adding unsupported claims. For example, change the second sentence to: "Experienced in designing and operating AWS cloud environments, building Terraform-managed infrastructure, and leading platform initiatives from implementation through production." This is supported by the EKS ownership, Terraform work, internal developer platform, and technical-lead experience already documented.
2. In the Core Skills section, move "Terraform" to the first position in the Cloud and infrastructure line and retain "AWS" immediately after it, so the most important infrastructure-as-code keyword is encountered earlier by ATS and recruiters. Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, or security tools, because they are not supported by the original candidate information.
3. In the Senior Platform Engineer entry, revise the first bullet to foreground both technical leadership and cloud-platform operation: "Technical lead for a five-person platform team, owning operation of an AWS EKS platform comprising 8 clusters and approximately 350 services across 3 regions." This more directly mirrors the requirement for leading technical topics while remaining faithful to the original wording.
4. In the Senior Platform Engineer entry, revise the internal developer platform bullet to make the system-design contribution clearer: "Designed and built an internal developer platform using service templates, Argo CD GitOps, and Crossplane self-service provisioning for RDS, SQS, and S3; reduced time to take a new service to production from approximately 2 weeks to under 1 day." The existing evidence supports both "designed" and "built" in this context.
5. In the Brightwater Games entry, change "Managed AWS infrastructure as code with approximately 40 Terraform modules" to "Managed AWS infrastructure as code using approximately 40 Terraform modules and Atlantis pull-request-based plan/apply workflows." This is more concise, preserves the existing evidence, and improves matching for infrastructure-as-code and delivery-workflow screening.
